claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by understanding your situation.

To determine your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to know about the child or children you're claiming for.

**First, how old is the child you're claiming for?** (or if you have multiple children, please tell me about the oldest first)

- Under 16 years old
- Between 16 and 19 years old
- 20 years old or older

Also, please let me know the child's name so I can keep track of the details.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So you're looking to claim Child Benefit for your son **Alex, who is 8 years old**.

Since Alex is under 16, that's great news - he automatically qualifies on the age requirement. Now I need to check a few more things to confirm your overall eligibility.

Let me ask you the next question:

**Is Alex working full-time?** (I'm asking because even though he's under 16, Child Benefit wouldn't normally be payable for a child working full-time)

- Yes
- No

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all. He's just in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Alex is in primary school and not working full-time, so that's all good.

Now I need to check some important eligibility criteria that apply to **you as the claimant**. These relate to your residency, work, and social security status.

**First, let me ask: What is your current residency status in the UK?**

For example:
- Are you a British citizen?
- Are you a citizen of another EU/EEA country?
- Are you a non-UK citizen with settled or pre-settled status?
- Something else?

This will help me understand which residency rules apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen and I live here in the UK.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Thank you for confirming that. Being a British citizen living in the UK means you meet the residency requirements for Child Benefit.

Now I need to check your work and social security situation. Let me ask:

**Are you currently working, or have you worked recently in the UK?** 

This helps me understand your national insurance record and whether you're in the right position to claim. Could you tell me:
- What is your current employment status? (e.g., employed, self-employed, not working, etc.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm currently working - I have a job here in the UK.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, thank you for that information. Now let me ask a bit more about your circumstances to complete the eligibility check:

**Do you have a National Insurance record in the UK?** (This means you've been paying National Insurance contributions through employment or self-employment, or you're currently paying them through your job)

Also, just to clarify your current situation:

**Are there any other children besides Alex that you'd like to claim Child Benefit for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, I have a National Insurance record - I've been working and paying National Insurance through my job.

And no, Alex is my only child, so I'm just claiming for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for confirming that. You have a National Insurance record through your employment, which is important for Child Benefit eligibility.

Now let me check one more important thing:

**Have you ever claimed Child Benefit before, or is this your first time claiming?**

Also, just to be thorough:

**Are you the person with primary responsibility for Alex?** (i.e., are you the main carer/the person with whom he lives most of the time?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
This is my first time claiming - I've never claimed Child Benefit before.

And yes, I'm the main carer. Alex lives with me full-time.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Thank you for that information. I now have all the key details I need to assess your eligibility.

Let me review your situation:

✓ **Child:** Alex, 8 years old
✓ **Age requirement:** Under 16 - qualifies
✓ **Working full-time:** No - he's in primary school
✓ **Your residency:** British citizen living in the UK
✓ **Your employment:** Currently working in the UK
✓ **National Insurance record:** Yes, paying through your job
✓ **Primary carer:** Yes, Alex lives with you full-time
✓ **First claim:** Yes, this is your first time claiming

Based on the Child Benefit eligibility rules, I'm pleased to tell you:

---

**You ARE ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex**

**Summary of eligibility:**
- Alex meets the age requirement (under 16 years old)
- He is not working full-time, so there are no restrictions on his eligibility
- You meet the residency requirements as a British citizen living in the UK
- You have an active National Insurance record through your current employment
- You are the primary carer with whom Alex lives full-time
- As this is your first claim, there are no issues with previous claims

**Next steps:**
You can claim Child Benefit through HMRC. You'll need to:
1. Apply online at www.gov.uk/child-benefit or by phone
2. Have information ready about Alex (name, date of birth, national insurance number if you have it)
3. Provide details of your income if it's over the threshold for the High Income Child Benefit Charge (currently £50,000)

Is there anything else you'd like to know about your eligibility or the next steps?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's brilliant, thank you so much! That's really helpful. I think I have everything I need now - I'll go ahead and make the claim online. Thanks for your help!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! I'm so glad I could help. You're all set to make your claim online for Alex.

Just to recap the key points for your application:
- **Child's name:** Alex
- **Age:** 8 years old
- **Your status:** British citizen, UK resident, employed with National Insurance contributions
- **Primary carer:** Yes, Alex lives with you full-time

Good luck with your claim! If you have any other questions about Child Benefit in the future, feel free to reach out. 

All the best! 🎉

All eligibility criteria are satisfied.

No factors prevent eligibility."
